To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) psychotherapy works, (b) psychotherapy works better than no psychotherapy, (c) different psychotherapies work for different patients, and (d) the best psychotherapy works best for patients with the best prognosis.
(1) psychotherapy works, (2) different psychotherapies work for different problems, and (3) the same therapy works for different problems.

1) psychotherapy is efficacious; 2) psychotherapy is specific to particular disorders, treatments, and patient characteristics; and 3) there is no evidence of a “dose-effect” relationship in psychotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of “how can we design clinically relevant psychotherapy research?”
the question, “What are the best psychotherapies for which patients?”
determining which of the many available treatments is appropriate for which of the many patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“psychotherapy works, for many people, for some problems, for some therapists, for a limited number of sessions, and under specific conditions” (see also Smith & Glass, 1977).
psychotherapy works for some people, for some problems, at certain times, in some settings, with some therapists, using some treatment models.
“psychotherapy works, and there is a psychotherapy that works for you”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we now know more about what does not work than what does.
psychotherapy works for some people with some problems and some therapists, but not for others.
the efficacy of psychotherapies depends on a number of factors: the nature of the patient, the nature of the disorder, and the nature of the therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the answer to the question, “Does psychotherapy work?” is a resounding, “Yes!”
we need to design psychotherapy outcome research that is relevant to the needs of the consumer.
the answer to the question “Does psychotherapy work?” is “Yes, but …”.
